# Arkenfall-Game

This is a text-based fantasy RPG inspired by DnD dice roll mechanics.

Status: Currently unfinished and a work in progress. Currently only the character
creation and opening of chapter one is playable. The combat system is partly built
and runs after the current lines of chapter one runs out.

How it works: Type your choices when prompted and press [ENTER] to advance
the story.

Features

Character creation:
- Difficulty sets the base stats: Easy (9 for each stat), Normal (8), Hard (7).
- 8 races: Human, Elf, Dwarf, Halfling, Orc, Gnome, Tiefling, Lizardfolk.
- 7 classes: Fighter, Rogue, Wizard, Cleric, Paladin, Ranger, Monk.
- 6 stats: STR, DEX, CON, INT, WIS, CHA – these are adjusted by race and
  class.
- Class decides the weapon proficiency, starting weapon, and starting spells (if
  Wizard, Cleric, or Paladin)

Combat (currently in development):
- Attack roll: d20 roll + stat modifier + proficiency + weapon rarity/magic master
  + attack modifier need to be higher than enemy AC (armour class).
- Natural 20 = critical hit.
- Natural 1 = critical miss.
- Damage roll: d6 roll + the same bonuses.
- 14 weapons, each with five attack styles (balanced, precise, heavy, reckless,
  signature) that trade accuracy for damage.
- 16 spells across two magic schools (arcane and divine) which are split into
  starter and learnable spells with mana costs.

Story:
- Chapter one: Woken by a nervous old man that will give the user the main
  quest and set the overarching goal of the program.
- To be continued. The user will progress through the story fighting enemies till
  they reach the end goal. The program will be split into chapters, and each
  chapter will end at the same point. If the character dies, the game ends. Other
  stats like CHA will be used in conversations to avoid confrontations or
  persuade people (e.g. get a better reward).
  
Note: This project was to really test myself and see if I could try to use a lot of
  different techniques I’ve learned and bring them into one project. The code has been
  through a lot of stages since I began, and I’ve had to change a lot because I knew
  less than I do now. The project will need a lot more work to become a neat complete
  project. If you want a smaller project like a quick card game that will be completed a
  lot sooner, I’m happy to try and create another project as the capstone and continue
  this one as a passion project.

# Arkengine

A typed asyncio Open Tibia server engine speaking protocol **8.60**, built as a
ground-up rewrite of a PyOT-derived engine. Milestone 1 ("walking skeleton"):
log in with OTClient, see the real map, walk around, see other players, chat,
with positions persisted.

## Architecture in one paragraph

A single asyncio process runs a fixed **20 Hz world tick** (`world/clock.py`).
The network layer (`net/`) decodes length-prefixed, adler32-checksummed,
XTEA-encrypted frames into typed commands appended to the world inbox; the
`World` (`world/world.py`) drains the inbox each tick, advances movement,
runs tick-scheduled tasks, and flushes one batched TCP write per session.
Content scripts register hooks with explicit imports and decorators
(`arkengine.scripting`) — nothing is injected into builtins. Persistence is
SQLAlchemy Core + Alembic (SQLite for dev, MySQL/Postgres by config), with
argon2id passwords and background save tasks that never block the tick.
The map subsystem (`world/map/`) hides behind narrow Protocols so a Rust
crate can replace the tile store, map-description serializer, pathfinder,
and frame codec later (milestone 4) without touching callers.

**New here? Read [docs/getting-started.md](docs/getting-started.md)** — a
zero-knowledge walkthrough from install to logged in. The full documentation
index (setup, in-game commands, combat/spells, running a server, content
authoring, and the wire protocol) is [docs/README.md](docs/README.md).

## Quick start

```bash
uv venv .venv && uv pip install -p .venv/bin/python -e ".[dev]"

# a small playable map ships in data/map-edited/ and is the default —
# nothing to copy to boot. (The full 2000x2000 world's .sec sectors are not
# in git; copy them into data/map/ and set ARKENGINE_PATHS_MAP_DIR=data/map
# to use it. See docs/getting-started.md.)

# create an account + character (applies DB migrations first)
.venv/bin/python tools/create_account.py myaccount mypassword --character Hero

# run the server (login :7171, game :7172)
.venv/bin/python -m arkengine
```

Point an 8.60-capable client (e.g. mehah OTClient) at `127.0.0.1:7171`,
protocol/client version **8.60**. The bundled OTClient hardcodes the standard
OTServ RSA key this server uses.

Config lives in `config/default.toml`; override in `config/local.toml`
(gitignored) or `ARKENGINE_<SECTION>_<KEY>` env vars
(e.g. `ARKENGINE_DB_URL`, `ARKENGINE_SERVER_ADVERTISE_HOST` for LAN play).

## Content scripts

Drop Python files under `data/scripts/`:

```python
from arkengine.scripting import TalkContext, on_talk

@on_talk("!pos")
def report_position(ctx: TalkContext) -> bool:
    p = ctx.player.position
    ctx.player_message(f"You are at ({p.x}, {p.y}, {p.z}).")
    return False  # consume; don't broadcast the say
```

Hooks: `on_startup`, `on_shutdown`, `on_login`, `on_logout`,
`on_talk(word, match="exact"|"first_word")`, `on_walk_on(item_id)`,
`on_walk_off(item_id)`. Handlers may be `async def`. Bad signatures fail at
boot, not at runtime.

## Verification

```bash
tools/check.sh                     # ruff + pyright (strict) + pytest
.venv/bin/python tools/smoke.py --map-only   # parse all real map sectors
.venv/bin/python tools/smoke.py    # boot real server, drive two headless bots
```

The integration tests run a real server on ephemeral ports and drive it with
a headless 8.60 bot client (`tests/bot/client.py`) that implements its own
framing and parsing, so server-side codec bugs cannot cancel themselves out.

## Roadmap

- **M2** — DONE (v0.2.0-m2): items & interaction — inventory/equipment, move with
  stack merge/split, containers (nested, multi-viewer), use items, stairs/holes/
  ladders/teleports, rotate, on_use/on_use_with hooks, inventory persistence
- **M3** — DONE (v0.3.0-m3 + follow-ups): monsters & combat — legacy genMonster
  files run as-is, lazy spawns, chase AI, melee, corpse/loot/exp, death respawn,
  skills with classic advancement, food/regeneration, item rarity (5 tiers,
  per-drop rolls), extended-opcode channel + client tooltip module
- **M4** — Rust hot paths (PyO3): tile store, map describer, A*, frame codec + `tools/load.py` bot swarm for capacity measurement
- **M5** — protocol breadth (more client versions), NPCs, spells, channels, houses

## Website

`.venv/bin/uvicorn --factory arkengine.web.main:create_app --port 8080` —
registration, character creation, highscores (docs/website.md). Admin panel
is phase 2.

## Provenance

Data (map sectors, `items.json`) and the wire-format knowledge were extracted
from the legacy nexPy/PyOT engine; the code is a clean rewrite. See
`docs/protocol-860.md` for the file:line-verified protocol spec.

# Arkengine / Arkenfall — project context

Paste this into a Claude chat (or add it to a claude.ai Project — see the note
at the end) so I have full context while you're away from your PC.

---

## What this is

**Arkengine** is a typed, asyncio **Open Tibia server engine** speaking the
classic **8.60 protocol** — a ground-up rewrite of a PyOT-derived engine. The
game/world is branded **Arkenfall**. Single Python process, fixed **20 Hz world
tick**. The client is an **OpenTibia Unity** client (8.60) plus the assets in
`Clients/`.

Owner: Josh (solo dev). Machine: Ubuntu 24.04 desktop ("BeastPC").
Repo root: `/home/josh/Documents/arkengine`.

## Architecture (one paragraph)

A single asyncio process runs a 20 Hz tick (`world/clock.py`). The network
layer (`net/`) decodes length-prefixed, adler32-checksummed, XTEA-encrypted
frames into typed commands on the world inbox; `World` (`world/world.py`)
drains the inbox each tick, advances movement, runs scheduled tasks, flushes
one batched TCP write per session. Content scripts register hooks via explicit
imports + decorators (`arkengine.scripting`) — nothing injected into builtins.
Persistence is SQLAlchemy Core + Alembic (SQLite dev, MySQL in production via
`config/local.toml`), argon2id passwords, background saves that never block the
tick. The map subsystem (`world/map/`) hides behind narrow Protocols.

## Key commands

```bash
cd /home/josh/Documents/arkengine
.venv/bin/python -m arkengine          # run server (login :7171, game :7172)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests -q     # full test suite (~208 tests, all green)
.venv/bin/python tools/worldgen.py --seed 9 --size 160 --out data/map-small
```

Production DB is **MySQL** at `192.168.68.90` (per `config/local.toml`), NOT
the local sqlite `arkengine.db`. The `josh` account is role 2 (god/admin).

## Directory map

- `src/arkengine/` — engine: `world/` (tick, combat, movement, npc, monster,
  spells, map/), `net/`, `protocol/v860/`, `persistence/`, `scripting/`
- `data/` — content: `items/items.json`, `monsters/`, `npcs/`, `spells/`,
  `scripts/`, and generated maps (`map-gen`, `map-small`, `map-edited`)
- `tools/` — `worldgen.py` (procedural map generator), `sec_otbm.py` (map
  format converter), `harvest/` (data mined from real maps)
- `Clients/` — Unity client + 8.60 `Tibia.dat`/`Tibia.spr` in
  `otclient-main/data/things/860/`
- `GameTools/` — `rme/` (Remere's Map Editor, built for 8.60),
  `Map harvesting/` (GreedOT + PepperCorn real maps we mined)

## Map system

- Engine loads custom **`.sec`** sector files (32×32 tiles) + `info.toml`.
  Item ids are **8.6 server ids** (e.g. 919=mountain, 4526=grass, 405=wood

import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')
      res.setHeader('Cache-Control', url.searchParams.has('omgithub_live') ? 'no-store' : 'no-cache')
      const content = readFileSync(file)
      if (extname(file) === '.html' && url.searchParams.get('omgithub_live') === '1') {
        const html = content.toString()
        res.end(/<\/body\s*>/i.test(html) ? html.replace(/<\/body\s*>/i, `${livePreviewScript}</body>`) : html + livePreviewScript)
      } else res.end(content)
    } catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not found') }
  })
  server.on('close', () => { stopWatching(); clearInterval(keepAlive); buildWatcher?.kill(); for (const client of clients) client.end() })
  server.listen(Number(process.env.PORT || 3000), '0.0.0.0')
  return server
}
if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) await start()

=== playing-the-game.md ===
# Playing the game — combat, spells, and progression

This chapter explains **how the game actually plays**: how you attack, how
damage is calculated, how skills and levels grow, how to cast spells and use
runes, what happens when you die, and the extra reward systems. It is written
for someone who has never played, but every number here is the real value the
server uses.

If you just want to get logged in, start with
[getting-started.md](getting-started.md). For the exact chat commands, see
[commands.md](commands.md).

The world is **classless**: there are no vocations. Every character grows the
same way — pick your playstyle by which skills you train and which spells you
cast.

---

## Your character stats

| Stat | Starts at | Grows by |
|---|---|---|
| **Level** | 1 | Gaining experience (killing monsters). |
| **Health (HP)** | — | +15 maximum per level. |
| **Mana** | — | +15 maximum per level. Spent to cast spells; regenerates while fed. |
| **Soul** | 100 (max 200) | +1 every ~2 minutes while fed. Spent to conjure runes. |
| **Skills** | 10 each | Using them (see below). |
| **Speed** | 220 at level 1 | +2 per level (configurable). |

Every character has **seven skills**, each starting at level 10:

**Fist**, **Club**, **Sword**, **Axe**, **Distance**, **Shielding**,
**Fishing**.

You train a skill by using it. The higher a skill is, the more attempts the
next level takes — the curve is `tries = 50 × 1.1^(skill − 10)`. Shielding
trains twice as slowly; fishing trains faster.

> In this build, **melee combat uses only Club, Sword, Axe, or Fist**
> (whichever weapon you hold). The Distance skill exists but ranged weapons
> aren't wired into melee yet, and there is **no Magic Level** — spell power
> scales on your character **level**, not on a magic skill.

---

## Attacking and melee combat

1. **Pick a target.** Click a monster (the client sends an attack request).
   You'll keep attacking it automatically.
2. **Get adjacent.** Melee only reaches **one tile** (including diagonals) and
   only on the **same floor**. If you're too far you'll follow but not hit.
3. **You swing on a timer.** By default you attack every **2 seconds**
   (`attack_interval_seconds`, tunable per server).

**How much damage a swing does:**

```
max = round( (0.085 × weaponAttack × skillLevel + level / 5) × fightFactor )
hit = random(0 .. max) − monsterArmor / 2      (never below 0)
```

- `weaponAttack` is the attack value of the weapon in your hand (best of your
  two hands; bare fists use attack 7 and the Fist skill).
- `fightFactor` comes from your **fight mode** (set in the client):
  - **Offensive** → ×1.0 (most damage, least defense)
  - **Balanced** → ×0.75
  - **Defensive** → ×0.5 (least damage, most defense)
- Every swing **trains your weapon skill**. Taking a hit while holding a shield
  trains **Shielding**.

Damage shows as floating red numbers with a blood splatter; a blocked (0)
hit shows sparks. Monster health is shown as a percentage bar.

**PvP / safety rules:** you cannot attack gods (role 2); protection zones
(temples, etc.) block combat; "secure mode" prevents accidentally attacking
other players.

The wire-level details are in
[protocol-860-combat.md](protocol-860-combat.md).

---

## Experience, leveling, and death

**Experience per kill** = the monster's base experience × your server's exp
rate (×2 more if it's today's [boosted](#daily-reward-loyalty-boosted-prey)
creature, and more again under an active prey hunt). In a party, experience is
split among nearby members.

**Level curve:** the experience needed for level *L* is
`50 × (L³ − 6L² + 17L − 12) / 3` — the classic Tibia formula. Each level up
grants **+15 max HP and +15 max mana**, refills you, and increases your speed.

**When you die:**

- You **lose 10% of your experience** by default (`death_exp_loss_pct`).
  **Blessings** soften this (8% less per blessing) and are consumed on death.
- Your items drop into a **corpse container**: your **backpack always drops**,
  and each equipped slot drops with a **10% chance** (reduced 2% per blessing —
  five blessings keep everything). A red-skulled (heavy PvP) character loses
  everything.
- You **respawn at your town temple**, fully healed, and the client relogs you
  shortly after.

Blessings, skulls, and the death penalty in detail:
[quests-pvp-social.md](quests-pvp-social.md).

---

## Loot and item rarity

When a monster dies it leaves a **corpse** you can open. Each possible drop is
rolled against its chance (multiplied by your server's loot rate, doubled for
boosted creatures). Corpses decay after about a minute.

Every piece of **equipment** (anything with attack, defense, or armor) is
rolled a **rarity** when it drops:

| Tier | Chance | Stat multiplier | Colour |
|---|---|---|---|
| Common | 79.5% | ×1.00 | white |
| Uncommon | 13% | ×1.10 | green |
| Rare | 5% | ×1.25 | blue |
| Epic | 2% | ×1.50 | purple |
| Legendary | 0.5% | ×2.00 | orange |

A legendary sword hits meaningfully harder than a common one. Rarity is shown
through client tooltips and inventory borders (and a subtle light "aura" on
the item). See [custom-features.md](custom-features.md) for how rarity is
surfaced to the client. Turn on `!quickloot` to send drops straight to your
backpack.

---

## Spells

You **cast a spell by saying its magic words** in normal chat — there is no
special command. If you meet the requirements, the spell fires; if not, you
get a short refusal message and a puff of smoke. Bystanders hear the
incantation (this matches real 8.60 behaviour).

**Every cast checks, in order:** your **level**, your **mana**, (for rune
conjuring) your **soul** and a **blank rune**, then a **cooldown**. Cooldowns
are tracked entirely on the server — there are two: a per-spell cooldown and a
shared per-**group** cooldown (so all your healing spells share one timer, all
attacks another). If you're on cooldown you'll see "You are exhausted."

### The shipped spellbook

**Healing** (heal yourself; formula = `level × scale + random(low, high)`):

| Words | Name | Level | Mana | Heals |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `exura` | Light Healing | 8 | 20 | `0.2×lvl + 8–18` |
| `exura gran` | Intense Healing | 20 | 70 | `0.6×lvl + 30–60` |
| `exura vita` | Ultimate Healing | 30 | 160 | `1.2×lvl + 90–180` |

**Attack** (`TARGET` hits your current target; `AREA` hits a shape around you):

| Words | Name | Level | Mana | Type | Damage |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `exori vis` | Energy Strike | 12 | 20 | target | `0.25×lvl + 8–16` (energy) |
| `exori flam` | Flame Strike | 14 | 20 | target | `0.25×lvl + 9–18` (fire) |
| `exevo flam hur` | Fire Wave | 18 | 25 | area (wave) | `0.3×lvl + 8–20` + burn |
| `exevo vis lux` | Energy Beam | 23 | 40 | area (beam) | `0.4×lvl + 12–30` |
| `exori` | Berserk | 35 | 115 | area (3×3) | `0.6×lvl + 15–40` |

**Support** (self):

| Words | Name | Level | Mana | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `utani hur` | Haste | 14 | 60 | Speed = `base × 1.3 − 24` for 33 s |
| `utana vid` | Invisibility | 35 | 115 | Invisible for 200 s |

**Damage notes:** attack spells respect the target's **elemental
resistances** — a monster can be immune (shows a puff, takes nothing), resist
(half), or be weak (extra) to fire/energy/etc. Spell damage is also reduced by
the monster's armour and otherwise flows through the exact same
death/loot/experience pipeline as melee.

### Runes (the two-step magic economy)

Runes are the classic Tibia way to store a spell in an item:

1. **Conjure** the rune by saying a conjure spell. This costs mana, **soul**,
   and one **blank rune** (item id 2260), and gives you charged runes.
2. **Use the rune** on a target on the map (use-with) to unleash it. Each use
   consumes **one charge**.

| Conjure words | Makes | Conjure needs | Rune effect (on use) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `adori gran mort` | 3× Sudden Death | lvl 45, 220 mana, 5 soul, 1 blank | lvl 45: `2.0×lvl + 60–120` to one target |
| `adori mas flam` | 3× Great Fireball | lvl 30, 120 mana, 3 soul, 1 blank | lvl 30: `0.8×lvl + 20–50` in an area + fire burn |
| `adura vita` | 1× Ultimate Healing rune | lvl 24, 100 mana, 3 soul, 1 blank | lvl 24: heals `1.5×lvl + 100–200` |

Single-target runes hit the top monster on the tile you click; area runes
blast a shape centred there; healing runes heal the targeted player (or
yourself).

### Conditions (damage over time)

Some spells and runes leave a **burning / poisoned / energized** condition
that deals flat damage every 2 seconds for a number of ticks. Status icons
(poison, fire, energy, haste, in-fight, etc.) appear on your client. Note that
in this build **paralyze, drunk, and mana-shield are icon-only** — they show
but don't yet change gameplay.

The full spell/rune builder API (for writing your own) is in
[spells.md](spells.md).

---

## NPCs, shops, and the bank

Walk up to an NPC and **say `hi`** (within a few tiles) to get their
attention. Then:

- Ask about keywords they mention in `{braces}` (e.g. `job`).
- Say `trade` to open their **shop** — buy and sell with real coins
  (gold = 1, platinum = 100, crystal = 10000; change is made automatically).
- Say `bye` to end the conversation.

The **Bank** NPC understands `balance`, `deposit <n>` / `deposit all`,
`withdraw <n>`, and `transfer <n> to <name>` (both players must be online).
Your balance is stored on your character. Full NPC/shop details and how to
create your own vendors: [npcs-shops.md](npcs-shops.md).

---

## Quests

Quests come in two flavours:

- **Reward containers / one-time events** — e.g. a chest you can only loot
  once, tracked by a hidden per-character flag.
- **Tracked quests with a log** — open with `!quests`. A quest has missions
  that start and complete as you make progress (for example, "kill 5 rats"
  updates as you kill them).

Try the shipped example: talk to **the King** about the **Rat Problem**, then
go kill rats and watch `!quests` update. How quests are authored:
[quests-pvp-social.md](quests-pvp-social.md).

---

## Daily reward, loyalty, boosted, prey

These reward systems reward regular play. All are toggled/checked with the
`!` commands in [commands.md](commands.md):

- **`!daily`** — claim a daily gold reward with a 7-day streak bonus (paid into
  your bank balance).
- **`!loyalty`** — you earn one loyalty point per distinct day you play; higher
  tiers grant small skill/loot bonuses and a title.
- **`!boosted`** — one creature each day gives **2× experience and loot**.
- **`!prey` / `!prey activate`** — spend 5 charm points for **+30% experience**
  on your next 20 kills.
- **`!bestiary`** — killing creatures fills a codex and awards **charm points**
  (which fund prey hunts) at milestone stages.
- **`!codex`** — one window that gathers Bestiary, Prey, Rewards, and Loyalty.

The mechanics behind all of these are documented in
[tier-c-systems.md](tier-c-systems.md).

---

## Quick reference

| I want to… | Do this |
|---|---|
| Attack | Click the monster; stand adjacent; set fight mode in the client |
| Heal | Say `exura` (or a stronger heal you have the level for) |
| Cast an attack spell | Target a monster, say `exori vis` / `exori flam` |
| Make runes | Say a conjure word (needs blank runes + soul), then use the rune |
| See my position | `!pos` |
| Fix a glitchy screen | `/sync` |
| Sell loot | Say `hi` then `trade` to a shopkeeper |
| Bank my gold | Say `hi` then `deposit all` to the banker |
| Claim rewards | `!daily`, `!codex` |

# Custom features: extended opcodes, rarity, client modules

## Extended-opcode channel

OTClient supports arbitrary custom messages outside the Tibia protocol:
packet `0x32` + `u8 opcode` + `string payload`, both directions. Arkengine
performs the enabling handshake at login (opcode 0 with an empty payload).

- Server -> client: `outgoing.write_extended(w, opcode, payload)`, or from a
  script `ctx.reply(payload)` inside `@on_extended`.
- Client -> server: scripts subscribe with `@on_extended(opcode)`; payload is
  capped at 8 KiB. Convention: JSON payloads.
- Client Lua side: `ProtocolGame.registerExtendedOpcode(op, cb)` to receive,
  `protocol:sendExtendedOpcode(op, json.encode{...})` to send.

Reserved opcodes: **0** handshake, **110** item tooltips, **111** rarity
overlays. Pick new features' opcodes in 112+ and record them here.

## Item rarity

Rolled per drop for equipment (attack/defense/armor > 0) in
`combat._drop_corpse`; stored as `attrs["rarity"]` on the item instance
(persists via the inventory JSON). `world/rarity.py` is the single source:

| tier | weight | stat multiplier | color |
|---|---|---|---|
| common | 79.5% | x1.00 | #ffffff |
| uncommon | 13% | x1.10 | #1eff00 |
| rare | 5% | x1.25 | #0070dd |
| epic | 2% | x1.50 | #a335ee |
| legendary | 0.5% | x2.00 | #ff8000 |

`Item.attack/.defense/.armor` return SCALED values — combat and tooltips use
these, never `item.type.*` directly. Look text and loot messages append
`[Tier]`. Scripts grant rarity via `ctx.give_item(sid, attrs={"rarity": t})`.

## Tooltip feature (opcode 110)

- Client module: `otclient-main/modules/game_tooltips/` (registered in
  `game_interface/interface.otmod` load-later). On UIItem hover it sends
  `{"x","y","z","cid","stack"}` using the 0xFFFF inventory/container
  addressing (docs/protocol-860-items.md), renders the JSON reply as a
  cursor tooltip sized to content, flipped/clamped to stay on screen, with
  rarity-colored name + border.
- Server provider: `data/scripts/tooltips.py` resolves the reference
  (lenient stackpos fallback on map tiles) and replies:
  `{"name","rarity","color","atk","def","arm","weight","vol","desc","count"}`.

## Rarity overlays (opcode 111)

Server pushes (at most once per tick, whenever carried items change):
`{"inv": {"<slot>": tier}, "cont": {"<containerId>": {"<index>": tier}}}` —
every EQUIPMENT item (attack/defense/armor > 0) including commons — common
glows grey (#9d9d9d); non-equipment (coins, food) never glows. Built by `interaction.build_rarity_overlays`;
sessions flag `rarity_dirty` at every interaction that can change visible
items (login, moves, eat, give, container open/close/parent, container
add/update/remove). Client (`game_tooltips/tooltips.lua`) paints 2px
rarity-colored borders on inventory slots (semantic widget ids from
inventory.otui: helmet/amulet/backpack/armor/shield/sword/legs/boots/ring/
tools) and container item widgets, PULSING via a 200ms alpha cycle, and
reapplies 100ms after each update so freshly opened container windows catch
up.

## Rarity aura (protocol-native, no client mod)

Best equipped tier glows as a creature light (0x8D) around the player,
visible to everyone: uncommon (3,66 green), rare (4,89 blue), epic (5,154
purple), legendary (6,192 orange); none/common = light off. Recomputed with
the overlay flush (World._update_aura). LIMITATION: creature lights only
render in darkness — invisible under full daylight (world light 250). The
always-visible upgrade is a client-side sprite tint/shader driven by a new
opcode (112 reserved for it): planned next.

## Paper-doll window (client module game_paperdoll)

Ctrl+D toggles a window with a UICreature preview of the local player plus a
grid of equipped items, borders colored from the opcode-111 overlay data
(shared by game_tooltips via the ArkRarityOverlays global). Pure client-side.

## Adding a new server-driven client feature (the recipe)

1. Pick an opcode (111+), note it above.
2. Server: a content script with `@on_extended(op)` parsing JSON and
   `ctx.reply(...)`.
3. Client: copy `game_tooltips/` as a template — manifest + Lua that
   registers the opcode and drives the UI; add the module name to
   `game_interface/interface.otmod` load-later.
4. Test: the headless bot has `send_extended()` and emits `("extended",
   opcode, payload)` events — see tests/integration/test_tooltips.py.

## Day/night cycle (server-authoritative)

The SERVER owns world time — it must be identical for all players and
drives gameplay (light, later night spawns/NPC schedules). Clients only
render the broadcast light level (0x82); they never run their own clock.
`World._daynight_level()` computes a cosine curve over
`world.daynight_seconds` (config; 0 = permanent day): day = config
light_level (250), night = NIGHT_LEVEL (40), smooth dawn/dusk. Recomputed
once per second, broadcast via write_world_light only when the level
changes. Login sends the current level. GM `/time <0-100>` jumps the cycle
(25=noon, 50=dusk, 75=midnight, 0=dawn) via a time offset. default.toml
ships daynight_seconds=600 (10-min cycle) for visible testing; raise for
production.

Unity may layer prettier ambient tint/color-grading, but MUST key it to
the server light level — never a client-local clock.

# Chat commands reference

Everything you type in the game's chat is one of four things:

1. an ordinary **say** (other players nearby see it),
2. a **command** (starts with `!` or `/` and does something),
3. a **spell incantation** (a magic word like `exura` — see
   [playing-the-game.md](playing-the-game.md#spells)),
4. an **NPC keyword** (`hi`, `trade`, `bye`, … when standing near an NPC —
   see [npcs-shops.md](npcs-shops.md)).

This page is the complete list of category 2: **commands**. Commands are
implemented as content scripts under `data/scripts/`; you can add your own the
same way (see [scripting.md](scripting.md)).

A note on conventions:

- `!something` commands are generally **player-facing** features.
- `/something` commands are generally **staff** (Game Master) tools.
- **Privilege** is your account **role**: `0` = player, `1` = Game Master,
  `2` = god. Staff commands silently do nothing for a role that's too low.
  You set your role when creating the account (`--role`, see
  [getting-started.md](getting-started.md#3-create-your-account-and-character)).

---

## Player commands (anyone)

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `!pos` | Prints your exact position: `You are at (x, y, z).` |
| `/sync` | Fixes a desynced client — resends the map around you, your inventory, and your stats. Use it if the screen looks wrong. |
| `!quests` | Opens your **quest log** window. |
| `!bestiary` | Shows your charm points and your most-tracked creatures with kill counts and progress titles. |
| `!daily` | Claims your **daily reward** (gold, with a 7-day streak bonus). Once per day. |
| `!loyalty` | Shows your loyalty points, title, bonus %, and points to the next tier. Loyalty rises one point per distinct day you play. |
| `!boosted` | Announces today's **boosted creature** (gives 2× experience and 2× loot today). |
| `!prey` | Shows your active **prey hunt** status, or tells you how to start one. |
| `!prey activate` | Spends **5 charm points** to start a hunt: the next **20 kills** grant **+30% experience**. |
| `!quickloot` | Toggles **auto-loot**: kill loot is moved straight into your backpack. |
| `!codex` | Opens the **Ark Codex** window (Bestiary / Prey / Rewards / Loyalty tabs). |
| `!market` | Opens the player **Market** window. |
| `!guild …` | Guild management. See the subcommands below. |

These features are explained in gameplay terms in
[playing-the-game.md](playing-the-game.md) and in depth in
[tier-c-systems.md](tier-c-systems.md).

### Guild subcommands — `!guild <subcommand>`

Guild rank is **separate** from your account role. Ranks are **Member (1)**,
**Vice-Leader (2)**, **Leader (3)**.

| Command | Rank required | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `!guild create <name>` | — | Found a new guild (you become Leader). |
| `!guild info` | Vice-Leader+ | Show guild name, MOTD, and members. |
| `!guild invite <player>` | Vice-Leader+ | Invite an online player. |
| `!guild join <name>` | (must be invited) | Accept a pending invite. |
| `!guild leave` | — | Leave your guild. |
| `!guild kick <player>` | Vice-Leader+ | Remove a member (cannot kick equal or higher rank). |
| `!guild promote <player>` | Leader | Raise a member's rank by one. |
| `!guild demote <player>` | Leader | Lower a member's rank by one. |
| `!guild motd <text>` | Leader | Set the guild message of the day. |

Typing `!guild` with no subcommand prints the usage help.

---

## Game Master commands (role ≥ 1)

These do nothing for ordinary players (role 0) — the text is just treated as
normal chat. Give yourself role 1 to use them (see
[getting-started.md](getting-started.md)).

| Command | Syntax | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/i` | `/i <name\|id> [count]` | Spawn an item into your inventory by **name** (`/i sword`) or **server id** (`/i 2376`), optionally a stack `count`. |
| `/a` | `/a <tiles>` | Advance (teleport) `N` tiles in the direction you're facing, landing on the furthest existing tile. Default 1. |
| `/goto` | `/goto x,y,z` | Teleport to exact coordinates. |
| `/pos` | `/pos [x y z]` | With no args, reports your position. With args, teleports there (`z` defaults to your current floor; commas or spaces both work). |
| `/summon` | `/summon <monster>` | Spawn a monster (by name) one tile east of you. |
| `/npc` | `/npc <name>` | Spawn an NPC (needs a definition in `data/npcs/`) one tile east of you. |
| `/where` | `/where <name>` | Report the position of a live NPC or an online player. For NPCs it also prints a ready-to-paste `/goto`. |
| `/time` | `/time <0-100>` | Jump the day/night cycle. `0` = dawn, `25` = noon, `50` = dusk, `75` = midnight. |
| `!roll` | `!roll [tier]` | Test tool: gives you a sword of a given **rarity** (`common`/`uncommon`/`rare`/`epic`/`legendary`), or a random tier if omitted. Used to preview rarity visuals. |
| `!kit` | `!kit` | Gives a fixed **starter combat kit**: sword, plate armor, plate legs, steel helmet, battle shield, boots, and 10 bread. |

> **God (role 2)** is defined but not yet used by any command — role 1 (GM)
> unlocks all of the above. Role 2's only current effect elsewhere is that
> gods cannot be attacked by monsters or players. See
> [admin-guide.md](admin-guide.md#privilege-roles).

---

## What is *not* a command

- **Spells** (`exura`, `exori`, `utani hur`, …) are not registered as
  commands — you cast them by simply **saying the magic words**. The full list
  is in [playing-the-game.md](playing-the-game.md#spells) and
  [spells.md](spells.md).
- **NPC conversation** (`hi`, `trade`, `deposit 100`, `bye`) is handled by the
  NPC you're standing next to, not by the command system. See
  [npcs-shops.md](npcs-shops.md).
- **Movement, attacking, and using items** happen through the client (arrow
  keys / mouse), not by typing.

## Objective
- Build a low-end-device remix of the game “Arkenfall”, specifically optimized for a Redmi 14C with 8 GB RAM, as a playable browser game in this empty OMGithub PlayGround repo.

## Requirements
- Must be a remix of Arkenfall, not the original server/Unity client.
- Target low-end Android phones, especially Redmi 14C / 8 GB.
- Needs strong browser performance: low memory, capped FPS, no heavy assets.
- Must be mobile-first with usable touch controls, responsive layout, safe areas.
- Should include browser verification and screenshots before completion.
- User gave no further constraints beyond the one-line request.

## Decisions
- Interpreted Arkenfall as the Tibia-like MMORPG from `Tofame/arkenengine` (Arkenfall Project), and built an original single-player pocket remix called **“Arkenfall: Emberlight.”**
- Chose a zero-dependency static HTML/CSS/ES-module canvas 2D game: no WebGL, no frameworks, no external assets/fonts, no network requests.
- Rendering design: pre-baked static terrain canvas, tiny cached pixel-art sprites, 30 FPS default cap, adaptive render scale, pooled particles/texts, DOM HUD updates at ~10 Hz.
- Gameplay design: town hub (Emberhold), three-quest arc (rats → wolves → Ember Warden boss), NPC dialogue, auto-equip rarity loot, potions, two spells, smiting/upgrades, death/respawn, local save.
- Mobile UX: virtual joystick, attack/spell/potion buttons, tap-to-talk, keyboard fallback, safe-area CSS, touch-action lockdown.
- Added `?debug=1` debug API and `?selftest=1` self-test for verification.

## Work State
### Completed
- Explored repo and identified Arkenfall source context (`Tofame/arkenengine`, docs on combat/quests/rarity).
- Created `index.html` with title screen, HUD, controls, dialogue/settings/stats/death/victory overlays, inline SVG icons.
- Created `styles.css` with polished responsive fantasy UI, HUD, joystick/action buttons, overlays, low-end media rules.
- Created `js/config.js` with map data, tile definitions, buildings, NPCs, monsters, spawns, quests, rarities, gear names, smith prices, spells, XP curve.
- Created `js/sprites.js` with cached pixel-art player frames, NPCs, monsters, trees, rocks, bushes.
- Created `js/world.js` with deterministic map generation, collision, reachability repair, zone detection, and one-time terrain bake.
- Created `js/audio.js` with tiny WebAudio synthesized SFX.
- Created `js/game.js` (~2,200 lines) covering input, loop, combat, loot, quests, death, camera, rendering, HUD, dialogues, settings, save/load, victory, debug API, self-test, boot.
- Ran `node --check` successfully on all five JS files.
- Fixed town-wall generation gap bug and NPC palette hack (`sprites.js` now imports `NPCS`).
- Removed duplicate `TEMPLE` import in `js/game.js`, aliasing only `TEMPLE as TEMPLE_POS`.

### Active
- Browser validation has not started yet.
- Known suspected issue: several Stillwater lake slime spawn coordinates likely sit in water and will fail reachability; planned replacements: `(22,44),(8,55),(10,60),(28,58),(28,47)`.
- Mire wolf spawns may also land on water/marsh and need checking.
- Sellftest and map reachability must be run in a real browser.
- README still only contains the OMGithub badge block; needs replacing with game documentation.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Start static server via persistent tmux using `./start.sh` with `PORT=3000`/`APP_PORT=3000` and `RUNTIME_DIR` already in env.
2. Load `http://localhost:3000/?selftest=1` with `playwright-cli`, click Play, inspect console errors and `window.__ARK_SELFTEST__`/`#selftest-output`.
3. Fix any unreachable spawn/water issues, JS runtime errors, sprite alignment, or rendering bugs.
4. Capture desktop and mobile screenshots (`./capture.sh` with `CAPTURE_URL`/`CAPTURE_DIR=screenshots`), inspect images, and iterate on visuals/HUD/touch layout.
5. Test gameplay via `?debug=1`: movement, attack, spell, potion, dialogue, quest accept/turn-in, save/reload, death/respawn, boss victory.
6. Optionally run CPU-throttled Playwright measurement to substantiate low-end performance.
7. Replace `README.md` with game description, controls, low-end design notes, verification results, and preserved OMGithub block.
8. Review `git diff`, ensure no broken assets/console errors, and commit/push per workflow.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: full UI/overlay structure and script entry.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: responsive HUD, controls, overlays, mobile/low-end styles.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/game.js`: main engine, gameplay, rendering, UI, save, debug/selftest.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/world.js`: map generation/bake, collision, reachability, zone logic.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/config.js`: all game content/data.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/sprites.js`: pixel-art sprite caches.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/audio.js`: synthesized SFX.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/README.md`: still needs game documentation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh`: static server launcher used for verification.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/capture.sh`: desktop/mobile screenshot capture helper.
- `/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime/scripts/default-start.mjs`: static server behavior and supported project types.
- `/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime/scripts/default-capture.mjs`: how screenshots/auto-start work.

## Important Context
- Repo was initially empty aside from OMGithub workflow/config files; all game files are newly created and uncommitted.
- Git branch is `opencode/41258048079`; remote `origin` is `https://github.com/antoniobedran8-create/PlayGround`.
- `start.sh` runs `node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs"`; static HTML project is detected via `index.html`.
- Capture auto-clicks a visible button whose label matches `/^(start|play)(\s+(game|now))?$/`, so the title button is exactly **“Play.”**
- `?selftest=1` sets `window.__ARK_SELFTEST__` and document title to `SELFTEST PASS`/`FAIL`; debug API is exposed as `window.__ark` only when `?debug=1` or `?selftest=1`.
- Self-test checks: map size, start/temple walkability, NPC reachability, all spawn reachability, XP monotonicity, rarity weight sum, quest chain order, save round-trip.
- Current slime spawns in `js/config.js` are likely all in lake water; reachability self-test should expose them.
- Import fix already applied: `START, TEMPLE as TEMPLE_POS`; selftest still references `TEMPLE` and must be updated to `TEMPLE_POS` or re-imported.
- `js/game.js` uses `TEMPLE_POS` for respawn but selftest line still calls `TEMPLE.x`; runtime selftest will throw unless fixed.
- No browser screenshots exist yet; only planned.
